note: CATCH-UP RUN: Thursday 10 Sep 2026, researched ~18:10-18:50 SGT (an evening run, not the usual pre-Asia slot) after the prior run 4 Sep -- a 6-day/4-session gap covering Fri 5 through today. NY is currently Thu 06:10am (pre-market; the latest COMPLETED US session is Wed 9 Sep). Latest completed sessions elsewhere: HK/JP/KR/SG all closed today (10 Sep). Snapshot of what happened across the gap: Fri 4 Sep NFP printed a blowout +162K vs 55K consensus (unemployment held 4.1%), reviving a HIKE debate (not cut) for the Sep 15-16 FOMC as new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole tone squares off against Governor Waller's dovish dissent -- hike odds have run 48-60% through the week. The S&P 500 gave back its early-Sep rally over three sessions (4 Sep -0.38% to 7718.60, 8 Sep -0.58% to 7673.52, 9 Sep -0.48% to 7636.36, -1.44% cumulative from the 3 Sep high) as VIX rose steadily to 16.46; Monday 7 Sep was a US holiday (Labor Day) so any same-dated VIX print that session is a stale/settlement artifact, not a live reading. The 9 Sep leg was compounded by the Treasury tripling its long-dated debt buyback operation, pushing the 10y yield to 4.857% (highest since Nov 2023). The Hormuz/Iran war escalated rather than resolved: IRGC claimed fresh strikes on vessels including two US ships, Iran said it is 'ready for a more intense conflict' and rejected a US-proposed transit framework, Houthi forces struck Saudi energy facilities widening the disruption, and Eurasia Group now pushes any de-escalation to year-end -- Brent topped $100 for the first time in six weeks (BZ=F 95.52->101.21) and WTI cleared $96-97 (CL=F 91.30->96.05). Barrick Gold fully reversed its 2 Sep governance-driven -5.34% drop, rallying back above $49 by 9 Sep alongside a broad gold-miner surge on renewed haven demand (analysts had kept Buy ratings with targets well above the dip level throughout). Xiaomi (1810.HK) fell 8.9% on the week specifically -- its 7 Sep product blitz (Xiaomi 18 Fold, Sky Nomad EVs) failed to offset concrete operating weakness (revenue -11% y/y, first decline in ~3 years; EV deliveries tracking only 44.8% of the FY target; smartphone shipments -26% y/y) -- while Tencent (-3.9%) and SMIC (-5.6%) fell on the same shared macro (Fed/oil/yields) pressure as the rest of HK tech, which SCMP called its worst week in over a year; no new China stimulus/Politburo catalyst was found. US market internals deteriorated sharply: CNN's live Fear & Greed index fell to 36.3/Fear (from 64.7/Greed a month ago), %S&P500>50-DMA cratered to 36.97% (from 45.52%), and Wed 9 Sep's NYSE advance-decline was a lopsided 21.6%/75.9%. Crypto drifted lower (BTC -4.1% on the week to ~$77,944) even as crypto-specific Fear&Greed stayed in Greed (69) -- a notable sentiment divergence from equities -- while the Sep 15 CLARITY Act cloture-vote odds deteriorated further to roughly 10-25% across trackers (from an 82% February peak), landing the same day as the FOMC decision. PPI (due today, 10 Sep) and CPI (due tomorrow, 11 Sep) are both still pending as of this research and are the immediate swing data into the FOMC.

macro.regime: A blowout NFP revived a hike debate (not cut) for Sep 15-16, and a three-day equity pullback plus a genuinely escalating Hormuz war have turned the setup materially more two-sided than 4 Sep's dovish-pivot rally
macro.narrative: The week since the last run reversed much of the 3 Sep dovish-pivot rally. Friday 4 Sep's Non-Farm Payrolls blew past consensus (+162K vs 55K expected, unemployment steady at 4.1%), immediately reviving the case for a HIKE (not a cut) at the Sep 15-16 FOMC -- new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has held a hawkish line since Jackson Hole ('we have work to do') while Governor Waller remains the lone dovish dissenter arguing underlying disinflation trends are better than headline data suggests. Odds have run 48-60% for a hike through the week, a genuinely live, two-sided outcome. The S&P 500 fell three of the four sessions since (4 Sep -0.38%, 8 Sep -0.58%, 9 Sep -0.48%, Monday 7 Sep a US holiday), a cumulative -1.44% giveback from the 3 Sep high, with VIX climbing steadily to 16.46. Wednesday 9 Sep's leg lower was compounded by the Treasury tripling its long-dated-debt buyback operation, pushing the 10y yield to 4.857% -- the highest since November 2023. Separately, the Hormuz/Iran conflict escalated rather than resolved: the IRGC claimed fresh strikes on vessels including two US-linked ships, Iran publicly rejected a US transit-fee framework and said it is 'ready for a more intense conflict,' and Houthi forces struck Saudi energy infrastructure, widening the disruption regionally -- Eurasia Group now pushes any real de-escalation to year-end. Brent crossed $100/bbl for the first time in six weeks and WTI cleared $96-97, a genuine hot-war supply-risk premium rather than an OPEC or inventory-driven move. Gold and silver miners fully round-tripped their 2 Sep governance-driven dip: Barrick, which fell 5.34% on a Bloomberg report it was weighing delaying its North American IPO amid a shareholder revolt, rallied back above $49 by 9 Sep alongside a broad miners rally on renewed Hormuz-driven haven demand -- sell-side had kept Buy ratings and price targets well above the dip level throughout, consistent with an overreaction rather than a fundamental reassessment. Silver held a $66-68/oz range (+63% y/y). US market internals deteriorated materially over the week: CNN's live Fear & Greed Index fell to 36.3 (Fear) from 64.7 (Greed) a month ago, with Stock Price Strength and Safe-Haven Demand both reading Extreme Fear; %S&P500-above-50-DMA cratered to 36.97% from 45.52%, and Wednesday's NYSE advance-decline line was a lopsided 21.6% advancing versus 75.9% declining. Crypto drifted lower in sympathy (BTC -4.1% on the week to ~$77,944) even as the dedicated crypto Fear&Greed Index stayed in Greed territory (69) -- a genuine sentiment divergence worth flagging -- while the Sep 15 Senate CLARITY Act cloture-vote passage odds deteriorated further to roughly 10-25% across trackers (down from an 82% February peak), a hardening regulatory tail risk landing the same day as the FOMC decision itself. In Asia, Xiaomi fell 8.9% on the week specifically: its 7 Sep product blitz (Xiaomi 18 Fold, three Sky Nomad EVs) failed to offset concrete operating deterioration -- revenue fell 11% y/y (its first decline in roughly three years), EV deliveries are tracking only 44.8% of the full-year target, and smartphone shipments fell 26% y/y -- while Tencent (-3.9%) and SMIC (-5.6%) fell on the same shared global macro pressure (Fed/oil/yields) as the rest of HK tech, which one outlet called its worst week in over a year; no new China stimulus or Politburo catalyst emerged this week. Reuters separately reported some Chinese rare-earth suppliers have quietly refused shipments to US customers since early August even where valid export licenses exist, fresh confirmation of the ex-China rare-earth thesis ahead of Xi Jinping's planned 24 Sep Washington visit. PPI (due today, 10 Sep) and CPI (due tomorrow, 11 Sep) are both still pending as of this research -- the immediate swing data determining whether Warsh's hawkish camp or Waller's dovish camp prevails at the FOMC.
